'''Coke Stevenson Reed''' is an American mathematician and inventor from Austin, Texas.  He is the inventor of the proprietary Data Vortex network. Implementations of this network into [[supercomputers]] use a novel topology and switch logic based on his and [[Krystyna Kuperberg]]'s solution to a problem posed by [[Stan Ulam]] in the [[Scottish Book]].

Coke completed his Ph.D. at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] under [[Hubert Stanley Wall]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=18166|title = Coke Reed - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

==Biography==
Coke Stevenson Reed is an American mathematician and the inventor and Founder of Data Vortex Technologies, a privately held US company composed largely of former members of the United States defense community.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.datavortex.com/meet-the-team/ |title=Data Vortex Technologies – Meet the Team |access-date=2016-07-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170422145711/http://www.datavortex.com/meet-the-team/ |archive-date=2017-04-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In his work with the Department of Defense and Department of Energy, Reed developed a thorough understanding of the existing pitfalls of computer networks and performance. His career has included positions at the [[Institute for Defense Analyses]], Los Alamos National Laboratories, the United States Space Program, and the [[Microelectronics and Computer Technology Corporation]]. At Los Alamos, Reed worked in Physics and mathematics.<ref> {{Cite web|url=https://www.mathcomp.uni-heidelberg.de/fileadmin/Redakteure/PDF_Downloads/Data-Vortex-Talk_Bio-Reed_2015.pdf| title= Data Vortex Talk Bio Reed 2015 |date = June 16, 2015 | via= mathcomp.uni-heidelberg.de}}</ref> Reed received his PhD in 1966 under Dr. Hubert S. Wall at the University of Texas at Austin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://repositories.lib.utexas.edu/handle/2152/21021|title=Coke S. Reed Interview Transcript|first=Ben|last=Fitzpatrick|date=May 26, 1998|via=repositories.lib.utexas.edu}}</ref> His academic appointments have included the University of Texas, Auburn University, Georgia Tech, the University of Colorado Boulder, and Princeton University.

His contributions to national security were recognized in 1990 by the Department of Defense when he was awarded the Exceptionally Meritorious Civilian Service Award Medal.{{cn|date=September 2026}}

Reed has worked on implementation of the Data Vortex in novel spaces, such as exploration into knowledge-based computing, shared memory, and streaming dynamic graph analysis.{{cn|date=September 2026}}
